source.title: Towards Interpretability Without Sacrifice: Faithful Dense Layer Decomposition with Mixture of Decoders
source.authors: James Oldfield; S. Im; Yi-Xuan Li; M. Nicolaou; I. Patras; Grigorios G. Chrysos

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies sparse layer replacements and their specialized experts, but does not test superposition in the original model or any of the listed claim versions. Its results concern the proposed MxD decomposition, a related but different construct.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior findings about polysemantic neurons and distributed features as motivation, but those are not its own results. Its experiments measure MxD replacement fidelity, expert rank, and MxD feature evaluations; these characterize the proposed decomposition rather than whether the original model stores sparse features as overlapping directions.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes MxD sparse layer replacements and reports only its own method's fidelity, expert rank, probing and steering against Transcoder/SAE baselines. It cites polysemantic, distributed neurons (incl. Toy Models of Superposition) as motivation but measures no superposition, feature overlap, or polysemanticity in the original models. That is T4 (relies on the premise and reports its method's performance), not T6, since the sparse-decomposition premise is used.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct: the authors conclude that MxDs beat transcoders and skip transcoders on the sparsity-accuracy frontier. They also conclude MxDs learn similarly specialized features on probing and steering tasks. They make no claim about superposition in the base models.
record.recipe_differences: MxD replaces pretrained MLP layers with sparse mixtures of full-rank linear expert transformations. It does not use the original toy-model feature setup, feature geometry measurements, or sparsity/importance sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that fidelity varies with sparsity level K and encoder architecture/activation; MxDs perform better with GELU/GLU variants matching the base layer than with ReLU variants. Randomizing K during training reduces the shared-expert pattern with comparable reconstruction performance.

fits_no_version.finding: MxD layer-level sparse replacements with near full-rank experts (normalized rank 0.99) give lower downstream CE loss than transcoders and skip transcoders at all K.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse mixtures of full-rank linear sublayers approximate LLM MLPs more faithfully than neuron-level sparse decompositions at matched parameters.

record.problems: The experiments concern learned MxD replacements rather than native feature geometry in the original models. The paper reports no repeated-run uncertainty for its main fidelity comparisons; its checklist says training multiple models was infeasible for the largest runs. Several plotted results lack exact numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Sparse probing, feature-steering, output-generation matching, and additional-layer results are not included because they evaluate MxD/other replacement methods rather than the claim's original-model feature geometry. The appendix also reports ablations and additional results not cataloged here for the same reason.

untested.parts: No toy models, feature geometry, or sparsity-dependent transition.
No test of capacity competition or importance-based allocation as the cause of polysemanticity.
No alternative causes of polysemanticity examined.
No measure of feature spread across original-model neurons; transcoder/SAE baselines are compared only as methods, not as evidence of features in the LLMs.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features.
No test of feature dimensionality in the original models; expert rank concerns MxD weights.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/discusses is changed to T4/uses_without_test. The paper's motivation relies on polysemantic, distributed neurons, but it treats that as background rather than testing it. No verdicts are given. The Gemma2-27B results, probing, and steering are also method evaluations and are correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent geometric transition, or regular arrangement of superposed features is tested.
The paper does not test whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by limited representational capacity, nor whether feature importance determines which features receive dedicated dimensions.
No alternative cause of polysemanticity in the original models is tested.
The experiments evaluate features learned by MxD replacement layers, not feature distribution in the original LLMs or recovery of their activations by SAEs.
The paper does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The paper measures rank of MxD expert transformations, not whether the original model's superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional features.
